qa.q: Does the raw oldest-first trimmer actually fire before step 20 on real long runs?

qa.q: Can a single step's tool output exceed the gap between target and trigger, so the trimmer fires anyway?
qa.a: Unknown for this suite, but a 300-line file read is on the order of a few thousand tokens, so a 20k to 40k gap tolerates several reads. qa.decides: trigger on tokens only vs trigger on tokens plus per-observation masking of large tool outputs

qa.q: Is "keep the last few messages verbatim" sufficient, or must the first messages be kept verbatim too?
qa.a: OpenHands' condenser keeps the first N events (default 2, system prompt and task) and the last M verbatim and summarises only the middle, with self-reported no degradation, https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/arch/condenser. qa.decides: keep-last only vs keep-first-2 plus keep-last

qa.q: Will the summariser prompt obey a target size and a "keep the task" instruction?
qa.a: A parallel-compaction preprint reports summariser prompt instructions on content and size are largely ignored, https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2605.23296.md. qa.q: Does the 9-cell sweep fit the budget and separate the cells?
qa.a: 108 screen runs plus 36 for seeds 1 to 3 on the best cell is about 6 percent of the 2,500-run budget, which fits C7. qa.q: Could a higher trigger make stale-context failures worse?
qa.a: Plausible: a wider window keeps more pre-edit file views, and luka lists "re-reading a file after editing it, by rule" as untried. Every compression method scored worst on artifact and file-state tracking, 2.19 to 2.45 out of 5, https://factory.com/news/evaluating-compression. qa.q: Does the change touch short tasks at all?
qa.a: If short tasks never reach the trigger, the summariser never fires and short-task pass and cost are unchanged, which satisfies C6 by construction. nodes.cluster_name: Start-position reminder with eviction of old copies

qa.q: In the current default harness, does the original task text ever leave the context, or is it only lost under the abandoned 20-step summariser?
qa.a: Luka's note says the summariser dropped or shortened the task text in 6 of 10 read summaries, and that summariser was not kept. Whether the current default trims at all is not stated in anything I was given, and the CSV cannot answer it [C9]. If the task text never leaves the context in the current default, the start arm is identical to baseline and the idea does nothing.
qa.decides: trigger every N steps vs trigger only on the step after a trim

qa.q: Is there evidence that a goal placed at the start of a long agent context is attended as well as one at the end?
qa.a: Lost in the Middle reports a U-shape, with start and end both above the middle, but on multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval, not instruction following over 60 tool calls (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172). Arike et al. measured drift growing with context length in agents whose goal was already at the start, which is direct evidence that a start copy alone does not stop drift (https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AIES/article/download/36541/38679). So the baseline already is a start-position arm whenever the task text survives, which puts the burden on L1, not L2.
qa.decides: start position vs end position vs both

qa.q: Does replacing an identical copy at the same position every N steps change anything the model sees?
qa.a: If the copy is still there and unchanged, deleting it and reinserting the same text at the same position produces a byte-identical prompt. The schedule only matters on the first call after a trim removed the copy. A trim-triggered rule gives the same context at lower engineering and cache cost.
qa.decides: fixed every-N schedule vs trim-triggered reinsertion only

qa.q: What does inserting at position two do to prompt-cache cost?
qa.a: Prompt caching bills from the first changed token; everything after an insertion is a cache write at a higher rate than a read, 1.25 times base for writes versus 0.1 times for reads on Anthropic models (https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching). An insertion at position two forces a full-prefix rewrite each time, while appended copies at the end are read cheaply on later steps. The token count can be flat while the dollar cost rises, so C5 and C6 must be measured in dollars.
qa.decides: insert after the system prompt vs insert at the oldest surviving message after the trim boundary

qa.q: Will the start copy survive the trimmer, which the idea says is otherwise unchanged?
qa.a: A trimmer that drops or summarises the oldest messages hits position two first. Luka's summariser rewrote old messages into a summary, and that is where the start copy would sit. Without a protected flag, the start copy is the first thing eaten, which is the exact failure the PREDICTION names.
qa.decides: rely on position vs mark the copy as a protected message the trimmer skips

qa.q: How many seeds does the 12-task screen need for the 4-point kill threshold to mean anything?
qa.a: On 12 tasks one task is 8.3 points, so a 4-point threshold is below resolution with one seed. Five seeds per arm give 60 runs per arm, where 4 points is about 2.4 runs, still noisy but readable alongside the 20-run failure read. Two arms at five seeds is 120 runs, under 5 percent of the 2,500-run budget [C7].
qa.decides: one seed per arm vs five or more seeds per arm

qa.q: How is "lost the goal" decided in the 20-run read, and by whom?
qa.a: Luka's four failure kinds exist as labels, but the only labelled data I have is synthetic [C9]. A rubric must be written before the screen, for example: the final edits address a different requirement than the task text, or the agent's last stated objective omits a named requirement. Readers must not know the arm.
qa.decides: harness-assigned label vs blind human rubric fixed before the runs

qa.q: How does the idea interact with the retry-once default and with the short-task set?
qa.a: Retry is the kept default, so the keep rule baseline is 44 percent on the pair and the cost baseline already includes doubled cost on failures. A reminder that converts fails to passes lowers retry spending, which is a cost offset the measurement must capture. Short tasks under N steps never receive a reminder, so short-task pass should be unchanged by construction unless N is small.
qa.decides: measure against retry-on baseline vs retry-off

qa.q: Which role does the inserted copy carry, and does the API accept it there?
qa.a: A user-role copy right after the system prompt sits next to the original first user message, giving two consecutive user turns, which some APIs merge and others reject. Appending inside the system prompt avoids that but still rewrites the cached prefix. The pydantic-deepagents implementation uses a system-reminder tag inside a user message, truncated to 400 characters, which is a tested shape for the end position only (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vstorm-co/pydantic-deepagents@main/docs/advanced/periodic-reminder.md).
qa.decides: separate user-role message vs field appended inside the system prompt vs system-reminder tag inside the first user message

qa.q: Does the cost argument depend on position at all?
qa.a: Eviction can be applied to an end-position copy too: delete the previous reminder and append a fresh one, leaving one live copy. The idea's test confounds position with eviction, so a win on cost could be credited to position wrongly. A three-arm screen, or a two-arm screen where both arms evict, isolates position.
qa.decides: compare start-with-eviction against end-accumulating vs against end-with-eviction

qa.q: Do the saved logs of the 40 read failed runs contain the full tool output text and arguments, or only summaries and step counts?
qa.a: Unknown. Luka's file reports step counts, pass rates and failure labels but does not say what the logs hold. If outputs are missing, the replay collapses to a (tool, args) detector, which is a different rule from [F5].
qa.decides: replay the exact hash as specified vs build a cheaper proxy over (tool, args) only and defer output hashing to the screen

qa.q: In the 40 failed runs, how many are loop failures, and what share of all long-task failures do they represent?
qa.a: The idea states 9 loop runs among the 40 read failures, which would be under a quarter of failures. The synthetic CSV shows a similar share but must not be used as evidence [C9]. With long-task pass at 31 percent, converting even all loop failures would move pass by only a few points, so L4 is bounded from above.
qa.decides: carry the rule to screening as a primary idea vs file it as a secondary rule behind task-pinning or verification

qa.q: Does an interrupt message turn a looping run into a pass, or only end it sooner?
qa.a: The only measured evidence says no on pass rate: SWE-smith's warn-and-resample cut repetition but resolution stayed at 38.4 percent (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21798). Cognitive Companion cut repetition 52 to 62 percent at about 11 percent overhead but reports a repetition proxy, not task pass, and was neutral or negative on structured tasks (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13759). So the honest keep-rule claim is cost down and pass not lower, with pass up as the hope.
qa.decides: frame the rule as a pass-rate lever vs frame it as a cost lever paired with the existing one-retry default

qa.q: Will an exact hash on raw output ever match, given test runners print durations, timestamps and temp paths?
qa.a: Belief, not measured: pytest and most runners print wall-clock times, so two identical test reruns rarely produce byte-identical output. Without normalisation the detector fires late or never, and the replay will understate both recall and false positives. The replay should run both raw and normalised variants.
qa.decides: hash raw output vs normalise output before hashing (strip digits that look like timings, paths, PIDs)

qa.q: What legitimate repeats appear in passing long runs, and does threshold 3 clear them?
qa.a: OpenHands users report false positives on legitimate polling with hardcoded thresholds (https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/762), and pydantic-deepagents uses 3 as default with a warn-or-abort choice (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vstorm-co/pydantic-deepagents@main/docs/advanced/stuck-loop-detection.md). The replay answers this directly for this suite, which is the point of doing it offline.
qa.decides: one global threshold vs per-tool thresholds (higher for test and poll tools, lower for file reads)

qa.q: Should the count be consecutive repeats or repeats anywhere in the run?
qa.a: OpenRouter's doom-loop counter resets a streak when inputs change but not when other tools run in between (https://openrouter.ai/docs/agent-sdk/call-model/doom-loop-detection). Loops in SWE agents often alternate edit, test, edit, test with the test output unchanged, so a consecutive-only rule misses them. The replay should report both counting modes.
qa.decides: consecutive-streak detector vs run-wide count that survives interleaved calls

qa.q: At what step does the detector first fire in loop failures, and is that early enough to matter under a 60-step cap?
qa.a: Unknown until replayed. The entropy-collapse note claims exact repetition begins tens of turns after drift starts, so first fire may be late; the note's content was not readable and this rests on a search summary. If median first fire is past step 45, ending the run and retrying is the better use of the remaining steps.
qa.decides: interrupt with a rethink message vs interrupt by ending the run and letting the existing retry take over

qa.q: Are there enough passing long runs with full logs to form an equal set of 40?
qa.a: Unknown. At 31 percent pass on long tasks, the number of logged passing long runs depends on how many long tasks are in the 120 and how many seeds were kept. If fewer than 40 exist, the false-positive estimate has a wide band and the 10 percent kill line needs a stated interval.
qa.decides: equal-size matched set vs use all available passing long runs and report rates with a confidence band

qa.q: Does the replay cost anything from the 2,500-run budget or from calendar time?
qa.a: Zero suite runs, as the idea claims. Effort is a script over logs plus hand-reading of fires in passing runs to label them legitimate or not; belief: one to two person-days. That is cheap enough to finish before the screen.
qa.decides: run replay before the 12-task screen vs run it in parallel with the screen

qa.q: Could the interrupt message itself cause lost-the-goal failures, which luka's file shows rose when summaries dropped the task text?
qa.a: Luka reports that 6 of 10 summaries shortened or dropped the task text and lost-the-goal failures rose (agent-long-tasks_what_we_tried.md). qa.q: On the nine loop runs, does the first repeated cycle start before or after tool call 25?
qa.a: Unknown. F8 says passing and failing runs diverge after step 25, but divergence is not the same as loop onset, and the CSV that shows cycle counts is synthetic and cannot settle it [C9]. If loops start around call 15, the checkpoint fires after the cycle has formed and becomes a late nudge, which is the case the LangChain post says the model can ignore.

qa.q: Is the checkpoint a one-off injected message, or a persistent field the harness stores and re-shows?
qa.a: As written it is a one-off message, which means any later context trimming or summarising can drop it, and luka's summarisation trial dropped even the task text in 6 of 10 summaries. A stored state object survives trimming and gives the loop detector a fixed field to grade. The OpenRouter detector docs describe the escalation rungs but do not say where the expectation lives (https://openrouter.ai/docs/agent-sdk/call-model/doom-loop-detection).
qa.decides: plain injected message vs a structured state object the harness keeps outside the transcript

qa.q: Does the harness grade the expectation against the next test result, or is it text the agent alone reads?
qa.a: In the idea as stated, grading belongs to the loop detector, which the test switches off, so the screen measures write-only reflection. The test-aware pattern in the brief grades progress by failure count falling or flat, with no published threshold (https://www.agentpatterns.ai/observability/loop-detection/). Write-only is cheaper but is also the version most likely to do nothing.
qa.decides: grade and inject a mismatch notice vs write-only reflection

qa.q: Do short tasks reach 25 tool calls at all?
qa.a: Unknown. The material gives no step distribution for short tasks, and the synthetic sample only covers long tasks. If short tasks commonly pass 25 calls, C6 requires checking short-task pass in the screen rather than assuming it is flat.
qa.decides: one global threshold vs firing only in the long-task suite

qa.q: Is the counter tool calls or model turns, and does it reset on the retry run?
qa.a: The idea says tool call 25; the sample's steps column runs 38 to 61 per run, so tool calls and steps may differ by a factor of two if steps include text turns. Retry from scratch is the current default (luka), so each retry run has its own call 25, and the checkpoint fires twice per failed task, which doubles its cost on exactly the runs where cost already doubles.
qa.decides: count tool calls with a reset per run vs a per-task counter spanning the retry

qa.q: Can 36 runs per arm detect a one-third drop in loop failures?
qa.a: No. At the baseline rate, 36 runs yield about 3 loop failures per arm, so a third fewer is one run and noise. The screen must pick tasks that looped in F5's real data, not the synthetic CSV, or the refutation rule "loop-labeled failures unchanged" cannot be read.

qa.q: Where does the injection sit relative to the pinned task text and the system prompt?

qa.q: Does the agent act on "0 lines changed" when it is only an observation, or must the harness also block or warn?
qa.a: The nearest evidence says agents notice surprising observations far more often than they use them, 79-81 percent noticed against 37-50 percent used on Terminal-Bench and under 7 percent on AppWorld, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.17609. A bare diff is weaker than an injected solution, so expecting over half to switch is optimistic. The 12-task screen should log the switch rate; if under one third, add the harness message as a second arm.
qa.decides: pure diff view vs diff view plus a harness message like "same command, same output, change something before re-running"

qa.q: What counts as "the same command" for the diff key?
qa.a: Loop-detection guidance hashes exact tool-call inputs and treats a retry as justified only if parameters, context or plan changed, https://www.jetbrains.com/pages/ai-agents/architecture/ai-agent-loops/. Exact hashing misses `pytest -q` versus `pytest -q -x`, and the agent can trivially defeat it by adding a flag. Start exact, log near-misses, and widen only if the screen shows flag-jitter evasion.
qa.decides: hash of exact (tool, args) string vs normalised key ignoring flags, cwd and timestamps

qa.q: When the output changes, does the diff carry enough for the agent to debug, or does it hide the failing assertion?
qa.a: Unknown on this suite. A unified diff with 3 context lines drops the assertion message when only the line count or a timestamp changed, and test output often has nondeterministic lines (durations, ids). Normalise known volatile lines before diffing and always include full lines for any hunk containing "FAIL", "Error" or "assert". The kill criterion on tasks with changing output measures this.
qa.decides: pure unified diff vs diff plus the full text of any failing test block that appears in the diff

qa.q: How much of the context growth in long runs is repeated test output, as opposed to large file reads?
qa.a: Unknown on real data; the CSV lists files over 300 lines read but is synthetic [C9]. If a 2,400-token cycle repeats 4 times it saves about 8,000 tokens, which against a 60,000 to 70,000-token run is 10 to 15 percent, enough to delay one trim at most. Measure trimming events per run in the screen before claiming L4.
qa.decides: expect L4 to matter vs treat L4 as a side effect and sell the idea on L2 alone

qa.q: Does the diff view interact badly with the free-text prediction rule it keeps?
qa.a: They are complementary in intent, but the prediction rule compares expected to actual and now "actual" is a diff. If the prediction says "test_x will now pass" and the diff shows only "0 lines changed", the comparison is easier, not harder. Keep them separate arms in the screen so the panel can attribute effect, since combining would use 72 of 2,500 runs.
qa.decides: ship diff view alone vs ship prediction and diff together as one arm

qa.q: Does cheaper re-running encourage more re-running?
qa.a: Belief: a shorter observation lowers the per-step cost of looping, so a step-cap-bound agent may loop more steps before cap. Luka's note that raising the cap from 60 to 100 made loops longer, with cost up 45 percent, supports the worry. Log consecutive identical commands per run; if the mean rises against baseline, add a cap of 3.
qa.decides: diff view alone vs diff view with a cap on consecutive identical commands

qa.q: Where does the previous output live for comparison, and does it survive trimming or summarising?
qa.a: It must be harness-side keyed by command hash, outside the model context, or trimming would lose the reference and the diff silently reverts to raw output. This is allowed under C3 as memory between steps. Initialise empty, keep only the latest output per hash, cap stored size.
qa.decides: store last output per command hash in harness-side memory vs rely on the context window

qa.q: Could the agent read "0 lines changed" as "nothing broke, tests still pass"?
qa.a: Reflexion on MBPP shows self-judged signals without an external check misled the agent, 77.1 against 80.1 baseline, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.11366. A bare "0 lines changed" is ambiguous when the previous full output was trimmed. Show the outcome summary line with the diff; this costs about 20 tokens.
qa.decides: show "0 lines changed" alone vs show it with a one-line summary of the unchanged outcome, such as "0 lines changed; last result: 3 failed, 12 passed"

qa.q: Is 36 runs enough to see a 6-point pass gain?
qa.a: At 31 percent base pass, 36 runs give about 11 passes, and a 6-point gain is 2 passes, inside noise. Pick the 12 tasks with the most repeated cycles in baseline logs and screen on the mechanism quantities from L1 and L2, then spend a full measurement only if the switch rate exceeds one third.
qa.decides: screen on 12 tasks at 3 seeds vs screen on 12 tasks chosen for known looping, measuring cycle rate rather than pass

qa.q: Does the diff view affect short tasks?
qa.a: Short tasks rarely repeat commands, so the expected effect is near zero, but a single-repeat short task that relied on a nondeterministic line in the output could lose information. Apply to all tasks for simplicity, and watch the short-task pass figure under C6; gating by step would add a confound.
qa.decides: apply diff view to all tasks vs only after step 20
